limits: Diagnose the frozen16s per-run0.5dB failure, without changing its result or threshold. Exact Gaussian moments predict finite mean-envelope-power variance; independent batched simulation and scipy lfilter reconstruction test it. Ensemble envelope moments are not loudness, a full mixed-source or physical engine model, and do not by themselves qualify timbre/C/driver adoption.
The exact Gaussian statement covers normalized squared envelope amplitude, not arbitrary filtered/mixed audio power
Empirical quantiles/exceedances use512 independent synthetic runs, not a guaranteed per-run bound
No per-WAV gain normalization, new synthesis model, hearing or real-engine causal validation

Frozen amplitude directions projected from one/multi-cycle windows on a common supported center range. Origins are sampling/window sensitivity checks, not independent recordings. Known stationary OSC plus stationary Gaussian noise and detuned OSC impose no source AM; true single-carrier AM is a separate control. Central-bin noise gain differs across windows; results are not interchangeable power budgets or physical modulation measurements. No new fit/runtime model or promotion.
Different windows change central-bin Gaussian-noise gain as well as leakage and smoothing; do not equate their variance or power
No-AM controls may have band/window beating; this does not identify the real reference cause
The single-carrier AM control validates sensitivity, not real multi-harmonic source separation
Mathematical and empirical ensemble checks do not replace the old per-run gate or establish perceptual quality
Known stationary-control variances/lag ratios are not fitted physical engine modulation parameters
Hann2/Hann4 central-bin noise gains and smoothing differ from rect1; no direct energy/variance replacement
Original fixed A is short and dynamic; the cause of all real temporal variations remains unidentified
Existing listening review pending; no new page, C test rerun, hardware or spatial acceptance
